item.title: Mets designate Dylan Ross for assignment, select Jefferson Rojas to major league roster, sign Chayce McDermott to major league contract
item.description: Dylan Ross | (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) The Mets have announced several roster moves, as the team has designated right-handed reliever Dylan Ross for assignment, selected infielder Jefferson Rojas to the major league roster, and signed right-handed reliever Chayce McDermott to a major league contract for the 2027 season. Ross was drafted by the Mets in the 13th round in 2022 and has spent the entirety of his professional career in the organization up to this point. He made his major league debut this year, a lone one-inning appearance late in the season. In Triple-A Syracuse, where he spent rest of the 2026 season, he had a 5.81 ERA and a 6.07 FIP in 48.0 innings of work. It’ll be interesting to see whether or not he gets claimed on waivers following the DFA. Rojas could very well be the Mets’ consensus top prospect heading into the 2027 season. MLB Pipeline already considers him to be the best prospect in the organization, and there’s a good chance he’ll top lists like the one that we publish here at Amazin’ Avenue and the lists of Baseball Prospectus and Baseball America. Our own Lukas Vlahos listed him as a lock to be added to the 40-man roster his offseason in a recent preview of the team’s roster decisions. McDermott threw 5.1 innings for the Mets at the major league level after the Mets acquired him in a trade with the Dodgers are the deadline. In total, he had a 5.87 ERA in 7.2 major league innings in 2026. He had a 3.92 ERA and a 3.82 FIP in 41.1 innings in Triple-A.

item.title: Senegal and Morocco lead Afcon qualifiers but Tunisia protest
item.description: Senegal were stripped of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title by a Confederation of African Football appeals board, and are awaiting the outcome of their own appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport [Getty Images] Senegal became the first side to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations before Cameroon and Morocco were among five others to join them with two games to spare - but there was penalty drama in Tripoli. Tunisia, who have appeared at a record 17 consecutive editions of Afcon, are at risk of missing out after a contentious 1-1 draw against Libya. Libya's penalty equaliser just before half-time sparked protest scenes lasting over five minutes as players and staff challenged the decision. The video assistant referee system is not used in Afcon qualifying, and Tunisia's remonstrating with the fourth official on the touchline ultimately only served to delay the spot-kick, which Ezoo El Mariamy, the player who was adjudged to have been fouled, converted. Drawing the game meant Tunisia's winless start in Group H continued, with the Carthage Eagles having just three points from four games. Tunisia need a strong finish to their campaign to give themselves a chance of reaching the finals, and Nigeria are also at risk of missing out, but others have made short order of qualifying. Led by new head coach Patrick Vieira, Senegal moved to the brink of a place at the finals by beating Sudan 4-2 on Monday, and the Teranga Lions had their passage from Group J confirmed on Tuesday when Mozambique secured a 1-0 victory away against Ethiopia. Cameroon and Benin also progressed without kicking a ball after Comoros and Burkina Faso registered wins - with the latter result also sealing a finals spot for the victorious Stallions. Mali and Morocco extended their perfect starts and booked their places with triumphs over Rwanda and Niger respectively. Abdellah Ouazane was the match-winner for Morocco in an away game that was actually played in Rabat, with the 17-year-old brilliantly curling in midway through the first half to cap a fine team move. The Atlas Lions and Senegal are still waiting for the outcome of a case at the Court of Arbitration for Sport to decide the destination of the 2025 Afcon title. Senegal won the final 1-0 after extra time but Morocco were awarded the trophy by a Confederation of African Football appeals board which decreed the West Africans breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them. Cameroon, Senegal and Benin close in on Afcon 2027 qualification Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years? Eleven sides had the chance to join co-hosts Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda at next year's finals when the fourth round of fixtures culminated on Tuesday. item.title: Houston Dash hire former Orlando Pride head coach Seb Hines to lead team
item.description: Seb Hines is the new head coach for the Houston Dash. He had been with the Orlando Pride. (Soobum Im/NWSL via Getty Images) Houston Dash president Angela Hucles Mangano hadn't interacted much with Seb Hines before starting the hiring process for the team's new coach. But she knew Hines, a former NWSL Coach of the Year and NWSL championship-winning coach, was someone the Dash needed to consider for the job. It took just one initial interview for Hines to stand out. Now the Dash have hired Hines as their new coach in a move that Hucles Mangano called a "massive statement" for the club that's been searching for a postseason breakthrough. "What was really appealing was Houston's a great challenge, and I've never been one to shy away from challenges," Hines said. Hines, 38, coached the Orlando Pride to the NWSL championship and the NWSL Shield in 2024. He coached parts of five seasons with the franchise before being dismissed at the end of August with the club in 12th place. Hines is the first Black coach to win a trophy in the NWSL. His 2024 Pride team started the season unbeaten in its first 23 games, and ESPN writer Jeff Kassouf ranked it as the third-greatest NWSL team of all-time in October 2025. "He's built a winner before," Hucles Mangano said. "He's been an NWSL champion. He's been a Shield winner. He's been a coach of the year. He didn't just win, but he built something that lasted." Hines grew up in England, playing most of his career in his home country for Middlesbrough F.C. in the English Premier League and the Championship. He moved to Orlando City SC in 2015, first on a loan then in a permanent move. After retiring from playing, Hines started coaching in Orlando City's academy before taking an assistant job with the Pride in 2020. He took over as interim head coach in 2022 before getting the full-time gig. "I'm ready for this next chapter in my life and my career," Hines said. "I feel I fulfilled everything that I could have done in Orlando." Hines describes himself as someone with a player-centric philosophy who believes that individual development means team development. Hucles Mangano said Hines is not a boisterous person but instead has a calm demeanor, which she thinks is similar to how she operates. She also noted that he is consistent in his approach, and consistency is a key to success in the league. "Being able to take even some of his personality traits and apply them is going to really go into how we start to become consistent, how we start to find the success that we're looking to achieve," Hucles Mangano said. "The hope obviously is that it happens very soon." Hines now joins a franchise that has been unsuccessful at building a championship contender since its first season in 2014. The Dash won the 2020 NWSL Challenge Cup during the height of the pandemic but has made the NWSL playoffs just once over its 13 seasons. The coaching position has also been a revolving door. item.description: Conor McGregor is a fan of Josh Hokit | Chris Unger, Zuffa LLC Conor McGregor might have finally met his match at the box office. Though it’s been a while since McGregor was in his championship prime, to this day no UFC fighter has been able to match his pay-per-view pull, with “Notorious” holding several UFC pay-per-view records as well as being one half of a crossover boxing match with Floyd Mayweather Jr. in 2017 that generated almost four-and-a-half million PPV buys. So when McGregor praises someone’s star power, it carries weight. Right now, McGregor is all in on breakthrough heavyweight fighter Josh Hokit, who fell short in his bid to become champion this past Saturday at UFC 334. Hokit fought Ciryl Gane for a hellacious 25 minutes, losing on the scorecards but undoubtedly gaining a legion of new fans for his incredible effort. With Hokit spending much of his time on social media calling for an immediate rematch, McGregor chimed in to show support to the 29-year-old American, calling him “outside of myself… the biggest draw in the UFC today!” See McGregor’s unedited statement below. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) | Getty Images Barcelona midfielder Rodri has confirmed that winning the UEFA Champions League is his team’s main goal, but played down suggestions that the Catalans are favorites for the title. “Objectives are different from labels. Barça’s goal is to contend for everything; beyond that, we don’t apply any labels to ourselves. I try to instill a sense of calm in the group—helping them understand that it’s still early in the season, that we need to raise our level and sustain it over time so that, by March or April, we’re still in the running across all competitions. That is when we will truly need to step up our game if we want to contend for everything,” he said in an interview with Diario SPORT . Barcelona have not won the Champions League in more than 10 years, including zero times since the Lionel Messi era ended. “Labels like ‘favorite’ don’t really mean much. In my opinion, it’s been a long time since this club won the Champions League—which is our most immediate goal and the one we desire most—so let’s forget about being favorites; we need to approach this with humility and raise our level of play,” the midfielder said. Rodri arrived from Manchester City in the summer transfer window after being instrumental in Spain’s FIFA World Cup title. “I’m very happy—I think it shows. Moving to a different city brings a lot of uncertainty. I had visited Barcelona a few times before, but it’s a spectacular city with an unbeatable climate. item.title: Red Sox Must Trade Jarren Duran To Fix Their Outfield Logjam
item.description: Gregory Fisher-Imagn Images The Red Sox have made their choice loud and clear. With Jake Bauers signed to a four-year deal, Jarren Duran’s path is blocked. The team needs to move on from their speedy center fielder now, not later. Waiting too long could cost them the return they deserve. Mark Feinsand put the situation in plain terms. “Duran is part of a crowded Boston outfield with Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu, and with Jake Bauers now on the roster, that group is only more congested,” Feinsand wrote. The math is simple. Four players cannot all start in the outfield. Someone has to go. The Numbers Tell a Rough Story Duran’s 2026 season was a hard fall from grace. He hit just .207 with a .266 on-base percentage, according to Sports Illustrated. That is not the breakout star fans remember from 2024. Back then, he led the league in doubles and triples. He posted a 9.0 rWAR that year. The drop in performance is real and it hurts his trade value. His strikeout rate jumped to 27.1 percent while his walk rate fell to 6.7 percent, per Royals Review . He failed to hit righties this year, even though he has always struggled against lefties. A player who hits lefties and righties poorly is a hard sell. The Red Sox should not wait for the market to dry up. They need to act while they still have leverage. Why Waiting Is a Bad Move Rivals are already circling. According to Royals Review, trade rumors involving Jarren Duran surfaced as The Royals reportedly looked to Boston for a potential solution last offseason. A year ago, reports showed Boston set a very high asking price for Duran by demanding Royals All-Star pitcher Cole Ragans. That price has likely dropped significantly after a miserable 2026 season. The window to get a fair return is closing fast. Feinsand argued that “Moving Duran — who is still arbitration-eligible for two more seasons — might be the most logical way to thin out that logjam.” The Red Sox have Roman Anthony and Ceddanne Rafaela ready to play. They do not need to keep a player who is fighting for a spot and hitting poorly. The trade should happen now to clear the way for the young talent. Sports Illustrated reported that Duran was chosen in the seventh round of the 2018 MLB Draft. It is time for the team to let him find a new home.

item.title: Mike Evans Achilles Injury: 49ers Hope For Return Against Vikings
item.description: Kyle Terada-Imagn Images The San Francisco 49ers offense looks different without Mike Evans. The star wide receiver has missed three games due to Achilles tendinitis. His last play happened in the second quarter of the Week 6 win over the Commanders. He missed all practice that week with soreness in his leg and a rib issue. The team still has no clear date for his return. Running back Christian McCaffrey knows this injury well. He missed the first eight games of the 2024 season with the same problem in both legs. The pain was worse on one side. McCaffrey calls it a compounding issue that gets bad fast. “It’s tough,” McCaffrey said. “It’s a compounding thing that can get worse really quickly and then it can be really debilitating. I had my own experience with it. I hated everything about it.” The injury can be debilitating. Why the Offense Struggles Without Him The numbers show why Evans is so vital. The 49ers average 6.4 yards per play without him on the field. With Evans, that number jumps to 7.2 yards per play. Without Evans, the 49ers remain Super Bowl contenders. With him, they could be the favorites. Tight end George Kittle feels the difference every time he lines up. “Everybody on the field, their life is easier because of how good he is and how much of a threat he is,” Kittle said. Coach Kyle Shanahan sees progress but holds back on promises. He said Evans has a chance to return soon. Before Week 10, Shanahan observed that Evans has “a chance” to return as soon as Sunday night against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. Shanahan said Monday when asked if Evans will be back at practice this week, “I’m hoping to, just not sure yet. Still too early.” He added that Evans is flying in with the group that stayed behind. The team will watch the next few days to see if he can practice. What the Injury Means for the Season The bilateral version of the injury is not what Evans is dealing with. His tendinitis is only in his right leg. The issue is still serious enough to keep him out of action. ESPN received remarks from Dr. Daniel Kaplan, an orthopedic surgeon at NYU Langone Hospital, regarding the nature of the condition. Kittle admits he has never felt more confident in an offense. He linked that feeling directly to Evans. “I’ve actually never been more confident in an offense than when I look out and I see Mike Evans … I’m excited to get Mike back, hopefully.” The 49ers need him to stay healthy for the rest of the year. Evans’ return date remains the biggest question for fans.

item.title: EJ Smith’s Practice Squad Deal Proves Chiefs Roster Depth Is Real
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs addressed their running back depth on Tuesday. Heavy.com reported that rookie E.J. Smith signed with the practice squad after being waived earlier in September. He played six years in college at Stanford and Texas A&M before joining Kansas City as an undrafted free agent. Smith was always a longshot to make the main roster with so many talented players ahead of him. Brashard Smith sits on injured reserve and Jayden Ott has a hamstring issue. Tight end Jared Wiley also has a fractured ankle from the win over the Falcons. Smith Wants To Build His Own Legacy Being the son of a legend brings attention, but Smith knows he must earn his place. He spoke about this pressure in a post from July 2026 that Heavy.com shared. He said, “Y’all know who my dad is—just making sure I pave my own path, doing it my way and learning from him—as a kid my dad always told me to build my own legacy.” Johnson Says He Is Hungry For More While Smith joins the squad, rookie Emmett Johnson is proving he belongs on the main roster. Johnson stepped up big when Kenneth Walker missed the game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. He scored two touchdowns and totaled 171 yards from scrimmage. Johnson told general manager Brett Veach he was not there to play around. Johnson said, “My mentality every single time I’m out there is to dominate, man. My whole career I’ve been overlooked, I’ve been doubted, and people have told me I wasn’t good enough.” Johnson was picked 161st in the draft, and he wears a hat with that number to remind himself of his journey. He told Veach on their first call that he wants to win a Super Bowl. Johnson added, “It’s been going well, but I’m super hungry, man, and I want to help this team win a Super Bowl. I’m not just here to make a couple of plays here and there.” Patrick Mahomes threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns against the Falcons. He faced a scary hit with elbows and knees but doctors cleared him to play. Mahomes admitted the hit felt uneasy, saying, “Anytime it’s elbows and knees it’s always scary because you just don’t know,” per Yahoo Sports. The team will face the Arizona Cardinals next on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 1 p.m. ET at Arrowhead Stadium.

item.title: Katie Fiso, Ehis Etute lift Oregon women to big win over Murray State
item.description: On several occasions this season, the Oregon women's basketball team has leaned on its star duo of juniors to overcome a slow start. That was the case once again Nov. 17, as the Ducks were sluggish out of the gates before erupting for a big second half. Katie Fiso poured in 31 points, and Ehis Etute scored 23 and grabbed 13 rebounds as the Ducks (5-1) trounced Murray State, 97-76, in a matinee at Matthew Knight Arena. Fiso, coming off a career-best 32 points in a Nov. 13 win at Maine, shot 12 for 18 from the field and was 7 of 7 at the free-throw line to set the tone against the Racers (2-3). She is averaging 21.3 points per game in six contests this season. "Just playing basketball; when I'm having fun, I feel like it's really easy," Fiso said. "I'm thankful for the gifts that God gave me to get downhill, be crafty, be shifty and at the end of the day, just hoop." Etute now has four double-doubles in six games this year. While Oregon struggled to stop Murray State early on, the 6-foot junior helped the Ducks keep pace, tallying 10 first-half points and 11 rebounds — six of which came on the offensive end. "She's just so strong. ... If there's a better offensive rebounder out there, I'd like you to tell me," Oregon coach Kelly Graves said. "Because I just don't think so." Murray State, which reached the NCAA Tournament last year after winning the Missouri Valley Tournament, ran its lead up to as many as nine points in the first half. Its early scoring surge was highlighted by a long, arcing three-pointer from Claire Johnson at the end of the shot clock to put her team ahead 37-28. As a team, the Racers shot 16 of 34 (47%) from the field in the first half, including 6 of 14 (43%) from three-point range. Oregon held them to 11 for 33 (33%) and 1 for 11 (9%) over the final two quarters. "We switched out defenses from our zone to our man; started trapping," Graves said of what changed defensively for the Ducks as the game went on. "We just got a lot more aggressive. ... item.title: Chad Johnson Admits He Was Wrong On Rookie Caleb Downs
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Chad Johnson has flipped his script on the Dallas Cowboys’ rookie safety. The former wide receiver admitted he was wrong to expect Caleb Downs to be the next Ed Reed or Troy Polamalu. That high praise came before the season, but the reality on the field tells a different story. Downs played through a painful loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. The 21-year-old finished with 11 tackles but missed on any big plays like a sack or interception. The defense gave up 584 total yards in that game. Christian McCaffrey torched the Cowboys for 161 receiving yards and 62 rushing yards. Fans were angry and former players spoke out. Johnson noted on The Nightcap Show that Downs is having more bad moments than good ones. He said the rookie year is going to be rough, especially when playing on such a struggling unit. At 393.8 net yards per game, the Cowboys hold the NFL’s poorest ranking. That kind of support makes it nearly impossible for any single player to shine. Play Calling Blamed for the Breakdown The blame for Sunday’s loss does not stop at the safety position. Former linebacker Leighton Vander Esch called out the defensive coordinator for a terrible call. With the game hanging in the balance, the scheme left Von Miller alone against McCaffrey. It resulted in a 66-yard touchdown that sealed the fate of the game. Vander Esch called it an “Absolute horrendous play call” per Pro Football Network . He added there was “Zero reason to have a D-end in coverage that late in the game, let alone vacate the whole middle of the field iso’d on the best receiving back in the league.” That single play led to a 66-yard touchdown for McCaffrey. It was his second receiving score of the night. The Cowboys offense tried to answer back, but the clock ran out before they could win. The 49ers gained 214 rushing yards and averaged 9.4 yards per play against the defense. Following this defeat, Dallas stands at 4-6 for the season. Executive Admits The Frustration The defense is not playing up to standard. Stephen Jones spoke to the media about the team’s struggles. He acknowledged the fans are right to be upset with the current performance. Jones said, “I certainly understand their frustration because there’s no doubt that we’re frustrated,” per ClutchPoints . He went on to state that the way the team is playing ball right now is unacceptable. He felt the fans certainly deserve better than what they are getting. The team opted not to make big moves at the trade deadline last week. Instead, they pressed forward with the same group that has failed to stop opponents. The NFC East is still open, but the window is closing fast. The lowly Tennessee Titans face Dallas next weekend in a critical home must-win matchup.

item.title: James Ruth Is Rewriting The Mavs Story With Real Fan Connection
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Dallas Mavericks Chief Marketing Officer James Ruth is changing the team’s approach by focusing on real fan connection rather than just game results. Mavs Moneyball reported on Tuesday that the organization is telling a fresh story under his leadership. The new strategy prioritizes the bond between the franchise and its supporters across the metroplex. Ruth believes sports act as a vital link that brings people together in meaningful ways. The shift is already visible in recent content produced by the team. A video titled “From Dallas with Love” features a blue rotary phone where fans dial 1-1 to speak directly to Kyrie Irving. One fan told Irving, “I have a son that adores you,” according to the Mavs Moneyball report. Another supporter added, according to Mavs Moneyball , “And we love your game, and we hope you have a phenomenal year, and you tear it up this year for the Mavericks.” These moments show a deep emotional investment from the fan base that goes beyond standard team updates. Ruth Brings Texas Roots to Dallas James Ruth returned to his home state after three years as the chief marketing officer for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He previously led the launch of Austin FC during the pandemic and completed his undergraduate work at SMU. According to Mavs Moneyball, Ruth, together with Collin Kim, the VP of Corporate Communications, currently heads a team of producers focused on narrating the Mavericks story. This team is creating content that captures the attention of fans who want to feel part of the journey. Ruth explained his vision in an exclusive interview with Mavs Moneyball. “What makes sports an amazing thing is the idea that it’s a community connector,” he said. He emphasized the chance to build collective moments within a city like Dallas, Texas. Ruth described the team’s role as a “connected device” that helps unify the local population through shared experiences. A New Era of Fan Engagement Social media comment sections show that fans are noticing this revitalized content effort. The approach moves away from dry statistics and focuses on the human element of the franchise. While team media content is not new, the quality and emotional resonance of the recent pieces stand out. The rotary phone video is a clear example of how the team is honoring its history while looking forward. Fans are thanking Irving for his leadership and calling him an inspiration after his recovery from setbacks. The Mavericks are using these tools to strengthen the relationship with their community. Ruth’s background in building Austin FC suggests he understands how to cultivate a loyal fan base from the ground up. The goal is to make every supporter feel like they have a special place in the heart of the organization. This fresh story being told in Dallas is already making an impact on how fans view the team.

item.title: Bears Run Game Needs Monangai Back To Win Big
item.description: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears know they must fix its running game to survive the cold months ahead. Head Coach Ben Johnson has made it clear that the offense will change tactics once the bye week ends. He told the media that the team needs to lean on the ground attack more as the weather turns into typical Chicago winter conditions. Per Windy City Gridiron , Johnson admitted that the current results are not good enough. He pointed out that in nine games, the Bears have only averaged four yards per carry in three of them. That number simply does not work for a team with playoff hopes. The coach said the team will look at what they do well and try to find consistency again. The Missing Piece Returns The biggest boost for the offense is the return of running back Kyle Monangai. According to Shaw Local , Monangai returned to practice on Monday following a five-game absence due to toe and thumb injuries. His absence has hurt the team badly. D’Andre Swift has done a great job filling in, but he cannot carry the load alone forever. The offense needs both backs to work together. Monangai was the spark that helped the team reach those high yardage totals earlier in the year. His return gives the Bears a chance to get back to the form they showed before the injury. Scheme Changes Are Coming It is not just about having the right players back. Johnson plans to tweak the playbook to help the run game. He mentioned that the team is different now compared to last year, but they can still use lessons from the previous bye week. The coach said he hopes to find specific areas to make more consistent. A year ago, Chicago’s adjustments during the bye led to five separate games with more than 150 rushing yards. They had not eclipsed 140 yards in any game before that break. item.title: Ilia Topuria’s orbital fractures were ‘half a millimeter’ away from being career ending
item.description: Aleksandre Topuria (R) assists his brother, Georgia's Ilia Topuria (C), as they leave after losing the lightweight title bout against US fighter Justin Gaethje during the "UFC Freedom 250" mixed martial arts event on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, DC, early morning on June 15, 2026. (Photo by Brendan SMIALOWSKI / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Ilia Topuria really meant it when he said his brother saved his career by throwing in the towel during their UFC White House fight against Justin Gaethje. Topuria took tremendous damage during his fight with Gaethje, breaking his nose and both orbitals across four rounds. Leading into the fifth round, Topuria’s older brother Aleksandre (himself a UFC fighter) made the call to stop the fight. In previous interviews, Topuria credited his brother with saving his career. And now in a new interview with La Gazzetta Georgia, he explained just how close he came to getting retired from the sport by Gaethje. “I don’t think I would have lost my eye sight, they would have managed to restore most of my vision after surgeries,” he said of the damage he took. “However, the problem would have been that I could never fight again. When your orbital bones are fractured and you undergo surgery, they insert titanium plates to repair them. Once those plates are in place, you can never take another punch to that area. I narrowly avoided surgery by half a millimeter.” “God saved me, and my brother saved my right eye,” he concluded. Topuria is now preparing for a return to action in April 2027, although it’s unclear who he’ll fight next. There’s a lot of money in an immediate rematch against Justin Gaethje, although the new lightweight champion has made it clear he’s not interested. More willing to fight Topuria is Paddy “The Baddy” Pimblett, a man who has been in a feud with “El Matador” for years. Whoever it will be, they’ve now seen that Ilia Topuria is mortal and can be defeated. How Topuria will bounce back from that reality remains to be seen, but we’re kind of hoping for his sake that the UFC doesn’t convince Gaethje to accept an immediate rematch.

item.title: Braves And Mets Chase Lefty All-Star Trevor Rogers For Rotation
item.description: Daniel Kucin Jr.-Imagn Images The starting pitching market is heating up fast, and the Atlanta Braves have a clear target. According to reports, the Braves, New York Mets, San Diego Padres, and Chicago Cubs have all shown interest in left-hander Trevor Rogers. Rogers faces a tough choice right now. He can accept a one-year deal worth $23.15 million from the Orioles or test the open market. MLB.com’s Jake Rill noted that Rogers must make this call by 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Nov. 17. If he stays, he gets paid big money for one year. If he walks, he could sign a longer deal with a team that needs his specific skills. The Orioles made the qualifying offer because they know his value is high. A Career Turnaround in Baltimore Why are teams so eager to sign a pitcher who struggled in years past? The answer lies in his 2025 season, which Sports Illustrated’s Yirsandy Rodriguez called the main reference for his current success. Rogers posted a stunning 1.81 ERA over 109 ⅔ innings in just 18 starts. He also recorded 3.3 fWAR at age 27, a number that screams All-Star potential. Now, he is the most coveted left-hander on the market after Tarik Skubal. The Braves need this kind of stability in their rotation. They have big names, but adding a healthy, dominant southpaw like Rogers would give them a top-three starter who can eat innings and keep games close. The stats from last year prove he can handle the pressure of a big league rotation. The Cost of Signing a Lefty Money isn’t the only hurdle for these four teams. The rules for signing a player who rejects a qualifying offer are strict. Rosenthal wrote that teams who went over the luxury-tax threshold last year must give up their second- and fifth-round draft picks. They also lose $1 million from their international bonus pools. The Mets, Cubs, Padres, and Braves all finished above that threshold, so the penalty is real for every club in this race. Despite the cost, the need for a reliable second or third starter is too great to ignore. If Rogers stays healthy and builds on his 2025 numbers, he could anchor a rotation for years. The Braves have the financial muscle to absorb the draft pick loss if they believe he can help them win a title now. Other teams might hesitate, but Atlanta has shown it will pay to get the job done. A Window for Contention The clock is ticking down for Rogers to decide his future. Joining a contender remains possible for the 28-year-old no matter which team secures the sweepstakes victory. For the Braves, this is about locking down a piece that fits their championship window. They cannot afford to let a pitcher with this upside slip away to a rival in the National League East. The Mets would love to pair him with their own stars, but the Braves have the track record of making bold moves.

item.title: Body of Melbourne Cup horse found dumped in Sydney skip
item.description: So You Are competing in the Melbourne Cup at Flemington Racecourse on 3 November [Getty Images] The body of a top Australian racehorse has been found dumped in a skip bin, hours after its trainer revealed the horse had died from colic. In a video shared online, only two weeks after So You Are raced in the Melbourne Cup, the deceased racehorse appeared to be lying in a large metal bin surrounded by other household rubbish in Sydney. Trainer Bjorn Baker - who shared news of the horse's death from colic on Monday - has said he was "deeply distressed" by the video, and called for a "full explanation". Racing NSW, the state's industry regulator, said a preliminary investigation had found the horse was later properly buried, but called the way its body was handled "completely unacceptable". "Like everyone who has seen the footage, I am deeply distressed by the handling of So You Are's remains," Baker said in an statement shared online. "He was a much-loved horse, and he deserved to be treated with dignity and respect after his death." So You Are had a successful run during spring, winning four times at respected races including the Rosehill, Randwick and the Bendigo Cup. The five-year-old recently finished eighth in the Melbourne Cup, which was won by Point of Law, a horse previously owned by King Charles III. The racehorse had received urgent treatment after a severe bout of colic, but was "unfortunately unable to be saved" and was euthanised under anaesthesia, Racing NSW said. "So You Are was then transported for burial, and was being held temporarily, awaiting burial, when these images were recorded," it said. Burial at a licensed landfill is typically recommended for animals that die from euthanasia due to the chemicals involved in the process, according to the racing body. "That burial, however, should have occurred in a timely and respectful manner," it added. In a statement, REC Equine Specialists - the hospital where the horse died - said a contractor had been hired to dispose of So You Are's body. "We did not carry out the burial ourselves, but we chose the provider and the arrangements, and we take full responsibility for that." "We have spoken with So You Are's owners and trainer to apologise personally." The company added that it had stopped using the contractor, and was reviewing its processes to make sure they know exactly how horses are handled after leaving their hospital. "No owner should have to go through what So You Are's connections have experienced this week. We will make sure it does not happen again." The video posted online by builder Gregg Jowett appeared to have been filmed at a public rubbish drop-off and landfill called Lucas Heights, in Sutherland Shire, south of Sydney. The waste management company that runs the landfill site said So You Are's body had been moved to a skip bin in a permitted area, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation reported. item.description: Jamie LeBlanc-Imagn Images Pete Alonso hit 43 home runs and drove in 113 runs while playing for the Baltimore Orioles in 2026, according to RotoBaller MLB . His numbers were dominant and eliminated doubts about his power in a new city. A Slow Start That Turned into a Surge Alonso did not begin his time in Baltimore with the same force he showed later in the year. He hit just .198 with only four home runs through the end of April, a rough patch that had fans worried about his long-term value. But the story changed quickly as the season wore on and his bat found its rhythm again. Per RotoBaller, he proved unstoppable late by blasting 20 home runs across his last 220 plate appearances of the year. This late-season explosion showed that his early struggles were just a blip rather than a sign of decline. Consistency That Fans Can Count On The 2026 season added another chapter to a career defined by steady power production. Alonso now has six consecutive seasons where he hit at least 34 home runs and drove in at least 81 runs. RotoBaller notes this streak positions him as arguably the most reliable power asset in fantasy baseball. His ability to stay on the field is just as impressive as his ability to hit the ball out of the park. In every season of his career, he has tallied no fewer than 635 plate appearances, with the 2020 campaign being the only exception. item.title: Jeremy Fowler explains the ‘whispers’ about Jimmy Garoppolo that make New England Patriots deal difficult
item.description: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images The New England Patriots have a quarterback problem to solve. Their former draft pick Jimmy Garoppolo is being touted as a surprise solution. Drake Maye’s injury in Week 10 has created a major problem for the New England Patriots. Backup quarterback Tommy DeVito struggled against the Detroit Lions. With the trade deadline now passed, the Patriots can only look at free agents to replace Maye, if required to. One name to emerge is former Patriots quarterback Jimmy Garoppolo, who began his career with the franchise between 2014 and 2017. NFL insider Jeremy Fowler was quizzed about the Jimmy Garoppolo possibility – and said he is doubtful whether the 35-year-old quarterback would want to return. Fowler pointed out that Garoppolo has not played in the league for 12 months, and has lived on the west coast since 2017. He told the Rich Eisen Show: “Yeah, you have Garoppolo. I haven’t heard anything hard and fast about them signing Garoppolo at this point. “The problem there is that there were whispers dating back to the spring and summer that he was semi-retired at this point. “So, does he want to get out of bed and go play in New England for a 5–5 team? You know, I think he was happy out in LA or playing for a West Coast team. “At one point, he was maybe going to play for the Cardinals, that fell through, and they pivoted and signed Gardner Minshew. So, I question how motivated he is at this point to play.” Fowler also pointed out that when Garoppolo was last in the league with the LA Rams, he was operating in a backup role. The Patriots may be looking for a starter for several weeks, depending on the severity of Maye’s injury. “He made a lot of money and, he was last a backup quarterback. So, we’ll see,” he added. Patriots short-term plans Fowler added that the New England Patriots’ current plans are to stick with backup Tommy DeVito. He said: “It sounds like at least in the short term, they’ll go with Tommy DeVito.” The Patriots are currently in a bye week, and so have a little extra time to figure out their next steps. There has been no update on Drake Maye so far, but NBC Sports speculate he sustained a fractured ankle. item.title: PGA Tour pressure cooker at Sea Island with cards and maybe the Masters on the line
item.description: NAPLES, Fla. — Keith Mitchell enjoys playing the RSM Classic at Sea Island because it’s a home game now that he lives in the Georgia coastal community. Even better is when he doesn’t have to cope with the pressure that comes with the final tournament of the PGA Tour season. Mitchell took care of that with a runner-up finish in Japan, and a top 10 in Mexico. He is No. 52 in the FedEx Cup Fall, making him a lock for $20 million signature events at Pebble Beach and Riviera. “I still want to play well this week,” Mitchell said Tuesday. “It’s a little bit easier without the extra added pressure.” That falls to so many others. The RSM Classic is the final tournament for players to finish among the top 100 in the FedEx Cup to secure full cards for 2027, a transition year to the new model of two tiers. Everyone from No. 93 (Kevin Roy) to No. 100 (Christiaan Bezuidenhout) is at Sea Island. Right behind is Billy Horschel, who fell out of the top 100 last week. That’s not the only bubble. The top 60 are assured two signature events to start next year, at Pebble and Riviera. Max Homa looked to be in good shape, until different winners and big moves bumped him out, and then he played his way back to No. 60 going into Sea Island. Ben Kohles, who only a month ago was trying to keep his card, suddenly is No. 61 after finishing runner-up in the Austin Championship on Monday. The other bubble is a little more complicated. The top 50 in the world ranking at the end of the year get into the Masters. Some players might not have another chance this year. Others might go to Australia or pull a Ryan Gerard and fly to Mauritius to try to lock up top-50 status. Rickie Fowler is not in the Masters field and is sitting at No. 49. He has played only once in the last three months and is not at the RSM Classic. Fowler received a spot in the Hero World Challenge, overlooked news because of the return of Tiger Woods. Harris English is at No. 47 and playing at Sea Island as is Austin Smotherman, a two-time winner in the fall who is at No. 50. Outside the top 50 but within range are 19-year-old Blades Brown (54) and Ben James, the No. 1 player from PGA Tour University with two runner-up finishes in the fall. item.title: After turnaround season, Purdue soccer coach departing for SEC program
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − Purdue soccer 's first NCAA Tournament match in five years will come under a head coach on his way out. Richard Moodie , who led the Boilermakers the last three seasons, has accepted the Tennessee women's soccer head coaching job. Moodie will continue to coach Purdue through the NCAA Tournament. The No. 4 seed Boilermakers host Southern Illinois at 2 p.m. Friday in the opening round. More: Purdue women's soccer NCAA Tournament résumé, opponent, match time After going 13-19-5 in his first two seasons at Purdue, Moodie helped transform the Boilermakers into one of women's college soccer's best stories of the 2026 season. Purdue went 17-2-3 and won the Big Ten Tournament championship to earn an automatic qualifying spot in the NCAA Tournament and enters the tournament as Division I's highest scoring team. Ironically, Purdue and Tennessee, which fired fifth-year head coach Joe Kirt on Nov. 2, could meet in the Sweet 16. Purdue athletic director Tommy McClelland took an aggressive approach to retain Moodie. In November 2023, Moodie was hired as Purdue's third women's soccer head coach in program history after seven seasons at Division I women's soccer at South Alabama, where he went 91-36-19. Moodie, a native of Scotland, played collegiately at NCAA Division II Carson-Newman, just outside of Knoxville, Tennessee. He later coach both the men's and women's programs at Carson-Newman. The financial commitments Purdue made in an attempt to retain Moodie will remain in place as the athletic department seeks Moodie's successor. Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier.
